column4: labialization: kʷ and ku̯ fold together
non-syllabic u: w, u̯ and u fold together
non-syllabic i: y, j, i̯ and i fold together
acute: accent (the palatals ḱ ǵ have rows of their own)
macron: length, compared only when both forms mark length somewhere
inverted breve above (the palatals k̑ g̑ have rows of their own)
Wiktionary's Proto-Italic *z (as in *korzō) is the voiced allophone of *s
first person singular of a causative *‑eō
third person singular *‑eti, a PIE verb's citation form
Wiktionary writes Proto-Italic y as j (*jekʷor)
Wiktionary writes Proto-Italic *f between vowels as its voiced allophone β (*proβos)
Wiktionary writes Proto-Italic *θ between vowels as ð (*arðōs)
Wiktionary writes Proto-Italic *χ between vowels as ɣ
Wiktionary writes Proto-Italic *χ as h (*hundō); PIE uses no bare h
palatal: ḱ and k are not folded
palatal: ǵ and g are not folded
